newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline weakens, but UK hoarding anticipated.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline weakens, but UK hoarding anticipated.

text.p: NWE gasoline softened on Wednesday as weekly U.S. data showed a sharp rise in gasoline stocks.

Eurograde barges traded $2.00 to $3.00 a tonne weaker at $200.50 and $199.25 a tonne fob ARA. But regular unleaded barges firmed slightly to trade at $192.75, narrowing an unusually wide spread between regular and premium material, traders said.
Figures from the American Petroleum Institute released after the close of trade on Tuesday showed a sharp rise in U.S. gasoline stocks last week of 6.51 million barrels.
But U.S. government figures released on Wednesday showed a smaller stock build of 4.7 million barrels.
June swaps were valued $3.00 weaker at around $201 a tonne, but the June/July spreads held firm at around +$4.00.
Traders said that the spread was well bid with a stock-build of early June barrels anticipated in the U.K. ahead of the mini-budget expected in mid-June.
The spread was well bid with traders expected to hoard duty-paid material ahead of an expected gasoline tax hike in the post-election budget.
The exact date for the budget has not been set, but the most likely date in thought to be June 10, with traders expecting a tax hike of two to three pence per litre.
